title: hotfix: stabilize SLO enforcer regional failover hysteresis ordering
author: Samira Patel
description: Production incident (SRE-77) uncovered an ordering/hysteresis bug in the SLO enforcer that caused rapid regional failovers and cascading load-shedding during a regional capacity spike. The enforcer's hysteresis comparator was non-deterministic under concurrent updates which allowed nodes to flip their local state out-of-order, producing transient over-aggressive circuit breaks and thrash. This hotfix makes the hysteresis update ordering deterministic, reduces windowing sensitivity, and adds guardrails to avoid concurrent state races. Changes are intentionally minimal and focused: a deterministic comparator, a lightweight per-region stabilization timer, new unit + simulation integration tests, observability improvements (new metrics and tracing tags), and a helm values tweak to enable the new stabilization by default in canaries. Checklist: - [x] Root cause analysis attached (SRE-77 notes linked) - [x] Minimal code changes, no state migration - [x] Unit and simulation integration tests added - [x] Canary rollout plan and observability dashboards updated - [x] Release notes and runbook update included Rollout plan: deploy to canary region for 2 hours (monitor slo_enforcer.hysteresis.thrashing_rate, circuit_break.count, regional_failovers), then gradual ramp with 30m observation windows. If regressions seen, rollback by reverting the helm value `sloEnforcer.hysteresis.enabled` to false. Related: ENG-1842 tracks long-term enforcer refactor.
